A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MiraGe: Editable 2D Images using Gaussian Splatting. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-reconstruction experiments on Kodak and DIV2K, image-editing demonstrations, physics simulations, and appendix ablations, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original reconstruction results, editing demonstrations, physics simulations, and appendix ablations reported in v2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same flat-Gaussian representation, GaMeS parametrization, Amorphous/2D/Graphite variants, mirror-camera objective, and editing procedures. No method component or algorithmic step changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use Kodak and DIV2K for reconstruction and retain the same editing examples involving Animals and generated images, along with the same 2D and 3D physics demonstrations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains WIRE, SIREN, I-NGP, NeuRBF, 3DGS, and both GaussianImage configurations. The GaussianImage/GS curve comparisons and qualitative comparisons with DragGAN and PhysGen also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The 24-image Kodak evaluation, 100-image DIV2K validation set, resolutions, and 2× bicubic downscaling are unchanged. Both versions retain the same metrics, Gaussian initialization counts, camera settings, and testing procedures.

E4.justification: Appendix A retains the mirror-camera ablations in Tables 2 and 4, initial-Gaussian-count analysis in Table 3, and the same editing and artifact case studies. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and performance curves. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4 and the graphical results match. For example, Table 1 reports MiraGe-100k PSNR of 59.52 on Kodak and 54.54 on DIV2K in both versions. Qualitative editing and simulation findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, triangle-to-Gaussian mappings, Gram–Schmidt construction, losses, projection relations, and Appendix A.2 quaternion expressions are mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reconstruction quality, editing 2D images within 3D space, and integration with physics engines.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the interpretations of mirror-camera benefits and quality/resource tradeoffs. The same limitations concerning missing backgrounds, editing artifacts, parameter requirements, and subjective artifact evaluation remain in Section 5 and Appendix A.

D1.justification: The GPU disclosures, GaMeS implementation details, quaternion construction, Blender and Taichi usage, compression information, license statement, and code/project access information are unchanged. The new acknowledgements add no technical reproducibility details.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Matching the bibliography across its shifted page breaks confirms that no references were added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 6, Acknowledgements, identifying project funding and support for individual authors, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgements move the References heading from page 8 to page 9 and redistribute bibliography text across pages 9–10. Figures 1–21 and Tables 1–4 retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 makes funding attribution more complete through the new acknowledgements, with a small accompanying reference reflow. The scientific explanations, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the revision produces no meaningful overall quality difference.
